CRM.rationale: CRM presents a compelling but nuanced case. The franchise is structurally dominant — #1 in CRM for 13 consecutive years with ~20% market share, 150K+ enterprise customers, and >95% recurring subscription revenue. Q1 FY2027 earnings were strong: revenue +13.3% YoY to $11.13B, EPS +52.2% YoY to $2.42 (reported $3.88 adjusted beating $3.13 consensus), and OCF of $6.70B. AI traction is real and accelerating — Agentforce ARR at $1.2B (205% YoY), combined AI/data ARR at $3.4B (200% YoY). The valuation is historically dislocated: PE of 18x is at the floor of its 365-day range (18–57x), earnings yield of 5.5% exceeds the 10-year Treasury at 4.45%, and the PEG ratio is sub-0.4 given +52% EPS growth. The $50B buyback and ~10% share-count reduction provide an EPS floor. However, the balance sheet has fundamentally transformed — total debt surged from $8.44B to $39.28B (D/E now 1.15x) following the Informatica acquisition, equity declined 44%, and segment softness in marketing/commerce/Tableau is real. The Q2 FY2025 OCF anomaly of $740M (vs $6.70B in Q1 FY2026) introduces cash-flow uncertainty. The $15B trailing FCF figure (from web sources) is encouraging but not independently verified in the raw data. The Anthropic ~$5B stake and upcoming IPO add optionality. Net: strong franchise at a historically cheap valuation with genuine AI momentum, but the leveraged balance sheet and segment headwinds cap conviction. Score reflects a solidly positive fundamental view tempered by balance-sheet risk and incomplete data on cash-flow durability.
key_factors: Dominant CRM franchise: #1 globally for 13 consecutive years, ~20% market share (4x nearest rival Oracle at 4.1%)
Q1 FY2027 earnings beat: revenue $11.13B (+13.3% YoY), EPS $3.88 vs $3.13 consensus (+$0.75 beat), cRPO +14% to $33.6B
AI traction accelerating: Agentforce ARR $1.2B (205% YoY), combined AI/data ARR $3.4B (200% YoY), 28.6T AI tokens processed (+152% QoQ)
Historically cheap valuation: PE 18x at floor of 365-day range (18–57x), earnings yield 5.5% exceeds 10Y Treasury 4.45%, PEG sub-0.4
Aggressive capital returns: $50B buyback authorization, $27B ASR reducing diluted share count ~10% YoY, ~1% dividend yield
Balance sheet transformation risk: total debt surged from $8.44B to $39.28B (D/E 1.15x), equity declined 44% — driven by Informatica acquisition
Segment softness: management flagged 'ongoing weakness in marketing and commerce and increased softness in Tableau bookings and renewals'
OCF strength but lumpiness: Q1 FY2026 OCF $6.70B (+3.5% YoY) but Q2 FY2025 OCF was only $740M, making annualization unreliable
Anthropic optionality: ~$5B equity stake in Anthropic (valued at $965B pre-IPO) plus $300M token investment; upcoming IPO as potential catalyst
Macro headwinds: hot CPI 4.2% and PPI 6.5% reigniting rate concerns; Oracle $70B AI capex announcement triggered sector selloff on 2026-06-11
